meta.title: My Bean Plants in Three Mugs

paragraphs: My Bean Plants in Three Mugs, posted by Leo. Teacher Kim gave every Explorer three bean seeds and three mugs. We wanted to find out how much water a bean needs. Beans grow fast, so they are good plants for a school test. I check my plants every day after football training. I look at the mugs for five minutes, and then I write the numbers. This post has the facts and the numbers.

I put one seed in each mug and filled it with soil. I wrote the number of each mug on a small card. Mug One got no water. Mug Two got twenty grams of water every day. Mug Three got sixty grams of water every day. I used a small kitchen scale for the water. All three mugs stood on the same shelf near a window. I did not move the mugs, because the light must stay the same.

The room was twenty-eight degrees every day, so the seeds were warm. The shelf had natural light from the window. A bean seed needs water, warmth, and air to start to grow. It does not need light until the first leaves come. This is an easy experiment for a beginner.

After five days, the plant in Mug Two had a green stem of two centimeters. On day seven, I saw the first small leaves in Mug Two. After ten days, the stem in Mug Two was eight centimeters tall. The stem in Mug Three was only five centimeters tall. Mug One had no plant at all. I checked every stem with a ruler.

The seed in Mug One did not grow, because a seed needs water. The plant in Mug Three grew slowly, because too much water is bad for the roots. The soil in Mug Three stayed wet and heavy for many days. Roots need air, too, and a lot of water pushes the air out. The best water for a bean was twenty grams a day. That is a fact for my mugs, but another plant may need more water or less water. Teacher Kim says that a good experiment changes only one thing.

Next, I want to try the plants in a warmer room and a cooler room. Coach Matt says that plants and football players both need water, but not too much. Which fact surprised you? I will post new photos next week. Tell us in a message!
